problems.locator: PDF p. 17, Results, Homogeneity, permutation-test methods; PDF p. 32, Figure 3 note
problems.quote: we conducted permutation tests (n = 5,000 permutations) comparing the maximum and minimum condition means for each metric.
problems.note: Use se_basis = unclear. The paper identifies condition-object sets as the units on which the clustering outcome is computed, but does not identify what is permuted or treated as independent when obtaining the reported uncertainty. The methods do not establish whether the permutations operate on people, ideas, or sets. Under the extraction-spec se_basis field notes and codebook section 10, an unestablished uncertainty unit is unclear. Knowing unit = set does not establish se_basis = set. The extraction itself acknowledges that the resampling unit is not described; its stated conservative choice of set is therefore unsupported. printed is null because the permutation unit is not stated.

summary: Checked all 16 estimates against the supplied 42-page PDF after reading the complete markdown conversion, including both appendices. Extracted every cited source page and recovered Tables A2-A3 with pymupdf.find_tables. Numerical entries, coefficient columns, printed contrast orientations, and full-model observation counts match their sources. Participant counts appropriately remain null because analysis-specific post-exclusion counts are not printed. Found three unsupported se_basis codes for the exploratory clustering permutation tests: the outcome unit is set, but the uncertainty unit is unspecified and should be unclear. No additional in-scope outcome or reported contrast was found missing. Existing notes appropriately retain the paper's narrative/table and cosine-formula inconsistencies and distinguish the maximum-minus-minimum permutation tests from separately reported pairwise tests.
